name: Address Autocomplete (Azure Maps)
tagline: Type an address, pick a suggestion, and every address column fills in — through Azure Maps.

limitations: The suggestions are canned, not Azure Maps’. The demo has no key to hold and no account to bill, so the Searching preset carries a placeholder key and the demo answers the control’s own two requests — geocode:autocomplete on each settled keystroke, geocode on a pick — from sample responses in demo/maps.json: the addresses this repository’s dev rig uses. Type part of one — 1 mic, redmond, raffles, rivoli, tlaltenango, unmapped — and the list appears; anything else gets No addresses match, which is what Azure Maps says when it has nothing. The event log names each call as canned, and nothing leaves the browser.

What the control does with an answer is real: the list and its keyboard handling, a pick filling the street, city, state, postal code and country, the second call for coordinates filling latitude and longitude, and the notice when Azure Maps cannot place an address (pick 10 Unmapped Lane). A refused key, a site the account’s CORS rule does not allow and rate limiting are not demoed; the screenshots above show them, captured from the dev rig.

Every state that never leaves the browser is real here too: typing writes the street column, Clear empties it and reports the clear, and the other columns show under the field when the preset fills them. So is the form around the control — a preset each for a read-only form, no access to the street, one secured column, a business rule’s error and a hidden field, set the way the platform hands them over: context.mode for the first and last, each column’s security and errorMessage for the rest. Those presets, and No key yet, leave the key empty, so the control makes no request — as it does on a form where the key is missing.

This is a premium control. The manifest declares external-service-usage for atlas.microsoft.com and its geographic and Government endpoints, so an app containing it needs Power Apps licences for its users. The demo does not change that and cannot show it.

presets.name: Searching
presets.description: Type part of an address — 1 mic, raffles, rivoli — and pick a suggestion: the street, city, state, postal code and country fill in, then the coordinates. The answers are canned sample responses, not Azure Maps.

presets.name: No key yet
presets.description: The control as it installs: no subscription key, so it explains itself under the field and behaves as a text box for the street.

presets.name: An address on the record
presets.description: What a pick leaves behind: the street in the field, the other columns as one line under it, and Clear to empty all of them.

presets.name: A read-only form
presets.description: The same address on a form the user cannot edit: the field shows it, takes no typing and offers no Clear. Flip Read-only in the toolbar to see it come back.

presets.name: No access to the street
presets.description: Field security denies reading the street column, so the value never reaches the control. It says so rather than drawing an empty field somebody might type into.

presets.name: One column secured
presets.description: The user may not read City. The street stays editable and the line under it leaves the city out, rather than hiding the whole control over a neighbour's column.

presets.name: A business rule's error
presets.description: A rule on the form has rejected the street, and its message sits under the field in the platform's error style. Typing still works; the rule decides when the error clears.

addressLine1.error: Enter the street as it appears on the invoice.

presets.name: Hidden by a rule
presets.description: A rule has hidden the field. The control draws nothing at all, which is what a canvas app relies on; on a model-driven form the section is hidden around it as well.
